items.title: Sudhir Chaudhary tells Delhi High Court he has removed posts misidentifying CJP protest activist

Senior Advocate Dayan Krishnan made the statement on behalf of Chaudhary and his production company, Essprit Productions, before Justice Tushar Rao Gedela . "I have taken it down on my own. We have taken a conscious decision to take it down...We have also written to social media intermediaries, saying that if any of our posts are there by third parties with you, please take them down also," Krishnan stated. He added that he had no objection if any directions are passed against social media platforms for the removal of the content. Justice Tushar Rao Gedela Sherawat has sued Chaudhary and DD News over a show aired on the public broadcaster on August 27, when Chaudhary alleged that during the CJP protest, Sherawat was talking about destroying Parliament and creating a Nepal-like situation in India. items.title: Kerala University’s draft to ban campus politics triggers row, SFI alleges it targets them
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A controversy erupted in Keralam after a proposal for the Students' Code of Conduct Regulations of the Kerala University recommended prohibiting student political activities across all college campuses and affiliated institutions. Titled the Kerala University (Students' Code of Conduct) Regulations, 2026, the document served as an initial draft of the University’s recommendations to the Kerala High Court, which is currently hearing a plea seeking prohibition of campus politics across the state. The draft, which prohibits political activities on campus, however allows academic discussion of political subjects under stated conditions. It also makes students liable for disciplinary action for engaging in any political activities. This leaked draft Regulations invited much criticism. Unlike several other Indian states where campus politics is strictly banned, Kerala has a vibrant, deeply rooted student movement integrated with various mainstream political parties. The matter is likely to be heard by a bench of the Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia on Wednesday. items.title: Karnataka High Court nominates two women advocates as co-opted members of State Bar Council
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has nominated Senior Advocate S Susheela and Advocate Vijayamma V as co-opted members of the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC). The nominations were made by Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru , after consultation with the elected members of the State Bar Council. A communication issued by High Court Registrar General M. Chandrashekar Reddy on September 10 confirmed the nominations. The move follows the Supreme Court's August 4 directions in Yogamaya MG v. Union of India and connected proceedings, under which Chief Justices of High Courts were empowered to nominate two women advocates as members of their respective State Bar Councils. The Supreme Court's directions were issued in the backdrop of concerns over inadequate representation of women in elected bodies governing the legal profession. The mechanism provides for the co-option of women members in consultation with elected members of the respective State Bar Councils. Meanwhile, elections for the posts of KSBC Chairman and Vice Chairman are scheduled to be held on October 1. September 22 is the last date for filing nominations. items.title: I can't be held liable for every social media post by DMK wings: MK Stalin to Madras High Court
items.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin has told the Madras High Court that merely being the head of a political party cannot make him legally responsible for every social-media post published by its various wings or functionaries [ Aadhav Arjuna Vs Stalin ]. Stalin made the submission in a counter-affidavit opposing applications for interim relief in a ₹1 crore defamation suit filed by Tamil Nadu Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Aadhav Arjuna. The suit was filed against Stalin by Arjuna over a DMK IT Wing post that linked him to a person accused in a ₹258 crore drug trafficking case. “ The mere fact that I am the President of the DMK does not render me liable for every post published through the social media accounts of the various wings/functionaries of the party," Stalin has contended. Stalin said that while he exercises administrative control over office bearers of the party’s various wings, this cannot translate into legal liability for their individual acts. He specifically denied instructing or approving any post linking Arjuna or his family to a person named John Britto or to a drug trafficking case. Arjuna's suit is pending before Justice K Go

items.title: Malayalam film It’s a Medical Miracle confronts male sexual violence, but panics midway
items.summary: Spoiler warning: This article discusses major plot points from ‘It’s a Medical Miracle’. In popular cinema, the male body is almost exclusively built as an instrument of hyper-action, unchecked power, or comically pathetic vulnerability. When it suffers, it suffers heroically — bruised and bleeding, but fundamentally unbroken. We know how to film a man being beaten, bloodied, or even killed. Cinematography has spent decades perfecting the art of masculine martyrdom. What Indian cinema rarely knows how to do is hold space for the male body when it is stripped of its authority and becomes the site of sexual violence. In Shyamin Gireesh’s fantasy thriller It’s a Medical Miracle (2026), starring Sangeeth Prathap and Sharaf U Dheen, the narrative offers a rare, horrifying departure from this norm. The premise begins as a quirky fantasy setup: Ruben (Sangeeth Prathap) wakes from brain death with extreme, painful hyperacusis, that is, amplified hearing that turns ambient noise into physical agony. He has also urged the Court to grant an interim stay on further proceedings pursuant to the September 8 order, until the High Court decides the matter. The proposed complex is to come up on about 25.55 acres with a built-up area of nearly 20 lakh square feet. The government has since clarified that the Pattinapakkam site has not received final approval. Minister Aadhav Arjuna said on September 20 that only a Government Order had been issued so far and that a final decision would be taken by Chief Minister Vijay after a Detailed Project Report examines the feasibility of the proposal. items.title: Fountain Court's Alex Taylor on choosing a 47-year career in clerking over joining Fulham FC at age 16
items.summary: In July 1979, a 16-year-old Alex Taylor had a decision to make: take up a football apprenticeship at Fulham FC or join Fountain Court Chambers as a junior clerk, the lowest-paid and least familiar option on the table. He picked clerking. After 47 years, one senior clerkship and a chambers that grew from roughly 20 members to 116, Taylor is preparing to hand over the reins to Sian Huckett, who takes over as senior clerk in January 2027. In conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja , Taylor traces the evolution of clerking, from a paper-and-diary era with no formal career path to a sophisticated practice built on business development and client relationships. He also speaks on Fountain Court's deepening ties with India and a growing pipeline of Indian instructions into both London and Singapore. [Watch Interview] Edited excerpts follow. Pallavi Saluja (PS): Can you tell us how you got into clerking and the fact that you started at the age of 16? Alex Taylor (AT): It was through a careers officer at school. items.title: Willkie Farr & Gallagher appoints Dharshini Prasad as London Chair of international arbitration practice
items.summary: Willkie Farr & Gallagher has appointed Partner Dharshini Prasad as London Chair of international arbitration practice. Prasad is an alumna of NUS Faculty of Law, Singapore. She earned her LLM from New York University School of Law. Prasad has been with Willkie as a Partner for over the last four years. She is triple qualified to practice in Singapore, England and Wales, and New York, and advises on complex multi-jurisdictional disputes, handling billion-dollar arbitrations globally across various industries. She serves as an arbitrator, sits on the LCIA Court and ICC UK Arbitration Committee, edits for the AAA Dispute Resolution Journal, teaches arbitration worldwide, and helped draft SIAC’s 2016 and 2017 Arbitration Rules. Alongside Prasad, Willkie has appointed Kristen Young as global co-chair of international arbitration.
